advances: This gives an exact projection-quantile prefilter that is necessary before either the scalar crossing-completion interval or the convex support-clearance test is relevant. It exhausts the two-parameter family obtained by keeping the previous generic rational endpoint triangles and the three row directions \(x,y,-x-y\), while allowing arbitrary row constants, arbitrary compatible middle bodies, and arbitrary crossing levels. No member of that family can have three genuine lower crossings. Thus moving the zero lines or changing the convex extension cannot rescue this six-vertex core; a surviving search must change the endpoint shapes or the row directions.

proof:
We first prove the general filter. Fix \(i\) and choose \(a_i\in I_i\).
By (2),
\[
\left|A_0\cap\{f_i\le a_i\}\right|
+
\left|A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a_i\}\right|
<t-k_i\le m,
\tag{10}
\]
where the last inequality is (3). Both nonnegative summands in (10)
are therefore strictly smaller than \(m\).

Put
\[
s_i=a_i-c_i,\qquad r_i=-a_i-c_i.
\]
The first cap in (10) is
\(A_0\cap\{\lambda_i\le s_i\}\). By the definition of \(q_i\), its
area being strictly smaller than \(m\) implies
\[
s_i<q_i.
\tag{11}
\]
The second cap is \(A_2\cap\{\lambda_i\le r_i\}\). Since \(A_2\) has
area exactly \(m\), this cap having area strictly smaller than \(m\)
implies
\[
r_i<\beta_i.
\tag{12}
\]
Adding (11)-(12) gives
\[
-2c_i=s_i+r_i<q_i+\beta_i.
\tag{13}
\]
Summing (13) and using \(\sum_i c_i=-1\) proves
\[
2=-2\sum_i c_i<\sum_i(q_i+\beta_i),
\]
which is (4). Notice that this argument uses neither convexity nor a
numerical approximation.

We now compute (1) for (5)-(7). The areas in (9) follow by the
shoelace formula. Put
\[
\rho=\frac mM=\frac{111819}{1997159}.
\]
For a triangle of area \(M\) whose three distinct projected vertex
values are \(\alpha<\gamma<\delta\), its lower-cap area at threshold
\(z\) is
\[
M\frac{(z-\alpha)^2}{(\gamma-\alpha)(\delta-\alpha)}
\quad(\alpha\le z\le\gamma)
\tag{14}
\]
and
\[
M\left(
1-\frac{(\delta-z)^2}
{(\delta-\alpha)(\delta-\gamma)}
\right)
\quad(\gamma\le z\le\delta).
\tag{15}
\]
These formulas follow by subtracting or retaining the similar triangle
cut off by the level line.

For \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3\), the sorted projected vertex
values of \(A_0\) are respectively
\[
\left(-\frac{1719}{1000},-\frac{333}{200},
\frac{1519}{500}\right),
\tag{16}
\]
\[
\left(-\frac{629}{1000},-\frac{203}{1000},
\frac{53}{250}\right),
\tag{17}
\]
\[
\left(-\frac{2409}{1000},\frac{1453}{1000},
\frac{961}{500}\right).
\tag{18}
\]
At the middle projected vertex, the first cap has area below \(m\),
whereas the second and third caps have area above \(m\). The exact
margins are
\[
m-
M\frac{27/500}{4757/1000}
=\frac{5972907}{134000000}>0,
\tag{19}
\]
\[
M\frac{213/500}{841/1000}-m
=\frac{151349991}{336400000}>0,
\tag{20}
\]
\[
M\frac{1931/500}{4331/1000}-m
=\frac{101813239}{122000000}>0.
\tag{21}
\]
Solving (14)-(15) at cap area \(m\) therefore gives
\[
q_1=
\frac{1519}{500}
-
\sqrt{\frac{29703625967}{1406450000}},
\tag{22}
\]
\[
q_2=
-\frac{629}{1000}
+
\sqrt{\frac{282119337}{14064500000}},
\tag{23}
\]
\[
q_3=
-\frac{2409}{1000}
+
\sqrt{\frac{13171271829}{14064500000}}.
\tag{24}
\]
The maximum projected values on \(A_2\) are
\[
\beta_1=\frac{669}{250},\qquad
\beta_2=\frac{2273}{1000},\qquad
\beta_3=-\frac{367}{100}.
\tag{25}
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_i(q_i+\beta_i)
={}&\frac{1279}{1000}
-\sqrt{\frac{29703625967}{1406450000}}\\
&+\sqrt{\frac{282119337}{14064500000}}
+\sqrt{\frac{13171271829}{14064500000}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
The three elementary rational comparisons
\[
\frac{29703625967}{1406450000}-16
=\frac{7200425967}{1406450000}>0,
\tag{27}
\]
\[
\frac9{400}-
\frac{282119337}{14064500000}
=\frac{34331913}{14064500000}>0,
\tag{28}
\]
\[
1-
\frac{13171271829}{14064500000}
=\frac{893228171}{14064500000}>0
\tag{29}
\]
show from (26) that
\[
\sum_i(q_i+\beta_i)
<
\frac{1279}{1000}-4+\frac3{20}+1
=-\frac{1571}{1000}.
\]
This proves (8), which contradicts the necessary budget (4).

For completeness, the midpoint polygon has cyclic vertices
\[
\begin{aligned}
&(-229/2000,1977/2000),\quad
(957/2000,93/100),\\
&(2857/1000,717/1000),\quad
(4541/2000,411/500),\\
&(-81/1000,497/400),\quad
(-7/80,299/250).
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
The sums of the first and fourth vertices and of the second and fifth
vertices differ, so it is not centrally symmetric. After multiplying
endpoint edge vectors by \(1000\), the nine determinants between an
\(A_0\)-edge and an \(A_2\)-edge are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
-51333&499272&-447939\\
-447175&-1137&448312\\
498508&-498135&-373
\end{pmatrix},
\tag{31}
\]
all nonzero. Their dot products with the three row normals
\((1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)\) are also all nonzero:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(4757,-426)&4757&-426&-4331\\
(-4703,841)&-4703&841&3862\\
(-54,-415)&-54&-415&469\\
(1186,-117)&1186&-117&-1069\\
(-1173,210)&-1173&210&963\\
(-13,-93)&-13&-93&106.
\end{array}
\tag{32}
\]
This verifies the claimed genericity and completes the proof.
statement:
Let \(A_0,A_2\subset\mathbb R^2\) be compact two-dimensional convex bodies with
\[
M=|A_0|>m=|A_2|>0.
\]
Let
\[
f_i(x)=c_i+\lambda_i(x)\qquad(i=1,2,3)
\]
be nonconstant affine functions such that
\[
f_1+f_2+f_3=-1.
\]
Thus \(\lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=0\) and
\(c_1+c_2+c_3=-1\). For each \(i\), define
\[
q_i=\inf\left\{
q\in\mathbb R:
\left|A_0\cap\{\lambda_i\le q\}\right|\ge m
\right\},
\qquad
\beta_i=\max_{x\in A_2}\lambda_i(x).
\tag{1}
\]

Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be any measurable finite-area set, put
\[
k_i=\left|K\cap\{f_i\le0\}\right|,
\]
and fix \(t\in\mathbb R\). Define
\[
\mu_i(a)=
k_i+
\left|A_0\cap\{f_i\le a\}\right|
+
\left|A_2\cap\{f_i\le-a\}\right|,
\qquad
I_i=\{a\in\mathbb R:\mu_i(a)<t\}.
\tag{2}
\]
If, for every \(i\),
\[
k_i+m\ge t
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
I_i\ne\varnothing,
\tag{3}
\]
then the exact projection-quantile budget
\[
\boxed{\ \sum_{i=1}^3(q_i+\beta_i)>2\ }
\tag{4}
\]
is necessary. In particular, (4) is necessary whenever all three rows admit the genuine lower-crossing setup in which the left tail has mass at least \(t\) and the strict-low set is nonempty.

Now take
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_0=\operatorname{conv}\{&
(-1719/1000,-203/1000),\\
&(1519/500,-629/1000),\\
&(-333/200,53/250)\},
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_2=\operatorname{conv}\{&
(149/100,109/50),\\
&(669/250,2063/1000),\\
&(1503/1000,2273/1000)\},
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
and
\[
\lambda_1(x,y)=x,\qquad
\lambda_2(x,y)=y,\qquad
\lambda_3(x,y)=-x-y.
\tag{7}
\]
For these data,
\[
\sum_{i=1}^3(q_i+\beta_i)<-\frac{1571}{1000}<2.
\tag{8}
\]
Consequently there are no real constants \(c_1+c_2+c_3=-1\), no measurable middle set \(K\), and no levels for which all three rows in (7) satisfy (3). This excludes, a fortiori, every rational convex extension satisfying three genuine lower crossings, the scalar completion interval, and all applicable support-clearance inequalities.

The endpoint pair in (5)-(6) is in the required low-ratio generic class:
\[
|A_0|=\frac{1997159}{2000000},\qquad
|A_2|=\frac{111819}{2000000},\qquad
\frac{|A_2|}{|A_0|}<\frac38.
\tag{9}
\]
Its midpoint body \(B=(A_0+A_2)/2\) is a six-vertex rational polygon of area
\[
|B|=\frac{777067}{2000000},
\]
is not centrally symmetric, has no common endpoint edge normal, and every endpoint edge is transverse to every row direction in (7).
